                     </ns0:gap> Notion, as a Believer, but in a more spe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cial, as an Apostle. Priests and Prophets in the Old-Testa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment are peculiarly called God's Servants, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 134. <ns0:hi>Amos</ns0:hi> 3.7. and so are Ministers in the New, 2 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 1.24.</ns0:note> of Jesus Christ, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 6.16. Act. 1.13.</ns0:note> brother of James <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">That <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> who was the Son of <ns0:hi>Alpheus,</ns0:hi> Matth. 10. He mentions his Brother to distinguish himself from <ns0:hi>Iudas Iscariot,</ns0:hi> and his Brother rather than his Father, because <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> was most famous in the Church, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 15. <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 2.9. and 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 9.5. as likewise to shew his Consent with his Brother in his Doctrine, and to make his Epistle the more acceptable.</ns0:note>, to them that are sanctified by God the Father <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Viz.</ns0:hi> As the prime efficient Cause of Sanctification, which he works in Believers by the Son, through the Spirit.</ns0:note>, and <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Joh. 17.11, 12, 15. 1 Pet. 1.5.</ns0:note> preserved <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Their Salva<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion, and Perseverance, and Deliverance from Dangers, not being in their own Power; he intimates, that Christ was ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pointed to be their King, and Head, and Keeper, the <ns0:hi>Author and Finisher of</ns0:hi> their <ns0:hi>Fait<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>,</ns0:hi> Heb. 12.2. and furnished with Power for their Protection, and Security, and that by him they were kept unto the Salvation purchased for them, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> by his powerful Operation, and gracious Influence ma<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ntain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing their Faith, and Union with himself.</ns0:note> in Jesus Christ, and called <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">With an effectual Calling, the beginning of their Sanctification, before-men<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tioned. The Copulative, <ns0:hi>and,</ns0:hi> is not in the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi>; and the words may be <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ead, <ns0:hi>sanctified by God the Father, preserved in Iesus Christ,</ns0:hi> as being <ns0:hi>called</ns0:hi>; and so <ns0:hi>called</ns0:hi> may be understood as going before the other two; and then the sense is, <ns0:hi>to the called, sanctified by God the Father, and preserved in Iesus Christ</ns0:hi>; or <ns0:hi>to them who</ns0:hi> being <ns0:hi>called, are sanctified,</ns0:hi> &c.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">2 Mercy <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Which is the Fountain of Reconciliation, and all the Grace vouchsafed you. See <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 1.2. and 2 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 1.2. and <ns0:hi>Tit</ns0:hi> 1.4.</ns0:note> unto you, and peace, and love <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Either he means God's Love to them, or their Love to God, and each other</ns0:note>, be multiplied <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Mercy in the Effects of it, Peace in the Sense of it; and either the Love of God in the Manifestation of it, or their Love to God and their Neigh<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bours in the Degrees, and Exercise of it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 Beloved, when I gave all diligence to write unto you <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">The Apostle here declares the first Cause of his writing to them, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> his own Inclination and Readiness, according to the Duty of his Place (as an Apostle; so <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>o do; <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> being of my self willing, and earnestly desirous to promote your Welfare, when absent from you, by writing unto you.</ns0:note> of the common salvation: it was need<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ful <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">The second Reason of his writing, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> the necessity of it, in respect of the Danger they were in, as follows, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 4.</ns0:note> for me to write unto you, and exhort you, that ye <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Phil. 1.27. 1 Tim. 1.18. & 6.12. 2 Tim. 4.7.</ns0:note> should earnestly contend <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">By Constancy in the Faith, Zeal for the Truth, Holiness of Life, mutual Exhortation, Prayer, Suffering for the Gospel, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> against those that would pervert the Gospel.</ns0:note> for the faith <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">The Do<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ctrine of the Gospel; Faith is taken for the Object of Faith.</ns0:note> which was once <ns0:note n="†" place="bottom">Either, once for all, because it was delivered by all the Apostles as the only unchangeable Rule of governing their lives, and obtaining Salvation, to which nothing is to be ad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ded, and from which nothing is to be taken away: Or, it implies, that it was therefore delivered to them that they might never forsake it, and that if they do, they miss of their Salvation, as being never like to have another way made known to them.</ns0:note> delivered unto the Saints.<ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>I. e.</ns0:hi> Those things which concern the Salvation of us all in common, or that Salvation which is common to us all; there being but one Salvation for all Believers, and one way to it.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="‖" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Viz</ns0:hi> by God, not invented by Men.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:598" />4 For there are certain men crept in unawares, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 9.21, 22. 1 Pet. 2.8.</ns0:note> who were before of old ordained <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Gr. <ns0:hi>Fore-written,</ns0:hi> i. e. of whom it was formerly written, or fore-told, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> by Christ and his Apostles: or rather, it is to be understood according to our Translation, <ns0:hi>before-ordain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed,</ns0:hi> viz. in the eternal Counsel of God; God's Decree being compared to a Book, in which things to be done, are writ<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ten down. This the Apostle adds to prevent any Offence that might be taken at the Wickedness of these Seducers; and therefore lets these Saints know, that tho such Men crept in unawares to them, yet it was not without the Providence of God so ordering it.</ns0:note> to this condemnation <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>Iudgment,</ns0:hi> and it may be under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stood, either of a reprobate sense, to which they who thus perverted the Gospel, were given up by God, according to his Pre-ordination; or of that Damnation he decreed should follow upon their Wickedness, in making Shipwrack of the Faith themselves, and subverting others. This seems best to agree with 2 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 2.3.</ns0:note>, ungodly men, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">2 Pet. 2.19.</ns0:note> turning the grace of God into lasciviousness <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Abusing the Doctrine of the Grace of God, and Benefits of Christ revealed in the Gospel, espe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cially the Doctrine of Christian Liberty, to the encouraging themselves and others in the vilest Lusts, 2 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 2.1.</ns0:note>, and denying <ns0:hi>s</ns0:hi> the only Lord God <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Ei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther this may be understood of the Father distinctly from Christ, expressed in the following clause; and <ns0:hi>only</ns0:hi> is put in not to exclude either of the order Persons of the Trinity from being God, but to exclude Idols and false Gods: Or, it may be understood of Christ, as well as the words follow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing; not only because there is but one Article in the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> relating to the whole Sentence, but because it seems best to agree with the parallel place, 2 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 2.1. which is most gene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rally understood of Christ; and because the Heresies of those times, which <ns0:hi>Iude</ns0:hi> cautions these Saints against, struck e<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />specially at the Godhead of Christ, which he therefore the more expressly asserts.</ns0:note>,<ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Tit. 1.16.</ns0:note> and our Lord Jesus Christ.</ns0:p>
